newsitem.title: MEXICO: MEXICO STOCKS SLUMP ON PROFIT-TAKING, DOW JONES.
newsitem.headline: MEXICO STOCKS SLUMP ON PROFIT-TAKING, DOW JONES.

text.p: The Mexican bourse sagged at the open as profit-taking weighed on a market whose volume was thinned by caution.

"The market gave us very good returns earlier in the week, but any pretext will do to take profits, so with the sharp fall on Wall Street, selling is inevitable," a desk trader said. The leading IPC share index .MXX was down 43.74 points, or 0.84 percent, at 5,151.55.
"It's not a sell-off, we're sliding on thin volume. Dealing is slow as it's a summer Friday," the trader added.
Trading volume .TV.MX of 7.4 million shares was swollen by a single cross-trade of 2.8 million.

Dealers said Telefonos de Mexico (Telmex) weighed most on the market and was down 20 centavos to 21.30 pesos. The telecom firm's ADRs were down 11/16 at 54-1/2, while the Dow Jones had slid 49.94 points to 8,138.06.
Market stragglers traded at thin volume filled the short gainers' list .PG.MX, traders added.
On the broad market, sliders outpaced gainers by 31 to five, out of 39 stocks traded in total.
